items.rationale: Remains of insured property (declared garden building) destroyed by the storm-thrown tree; material arising under 5.2.1(a) and 7.1.7(a). Priced as ordinary waste-wood disposal for a small shed roof.

items.description: Disposal of broken glass pane from shed
items.rationale: Glazing is a building component of the insured site installation (4.2.2); its remains are material arising under 5.2.1(a). Small disposal charge for a single pane.

items.description: Disposal of green waste (branches and foliage)
items.rationale: Storm-felled tree thrown onto insured property counts as material arising under 2.5.3(c) and 5.2.1(b); the clearance carve-back in 4.3(e) applies. Priced as green waste disposal for one large tree.

items.description: Disposal of tree root ball (single mass under 1 m³)
items.rationale: 5.2.1(b) includes the root mass of a felled tree where it is a single mass not exceeding one cubic metre; description and invoice both confirm under 1 m³. Modest disposal price.

Ground material is not material arising, however processed (5.2.1(d), 4.3(d)). 5.2.2 is not met: no reinstatement-related ground works and no making good, so this is standalone clearance and not indemnified.

Paving grit is ground material by definition (1.3) and excluded under 5.2.1(d). The paving around the shed is not a terrace adjoining the building, and nothing was made good under 5.2.2, so not indemnified.

Excavated soil is ground material (5.2.1(d)). Its disposal as a clearance measure standing on its own, with no foundation or reinstatement works and no ground made good, is expressly not indemnified under 5.2.2.
